original_question: Which chromosome contains the gene responsible for the hereditary connective tissue disease Marfan syndrome?
key_entities: hereditary connective tissue disease Marfan syndrome

final_qi.question: Which chromosome contains the gene responsible for the hereditary connective tissue disease Marfan syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: Marfan syndrome is caused by mutations in the FBN1 gene, which encodes the extracellular matrix protein fibrillin-1. The FBN1 gene is located on the long arm of chromosome 15 (15q21.1), making chromosome 15 the chromosomal location responsible for this hereditary connective tissue disorder.

final_answer.long_answer: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal-dominant connective-tissue disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the FBN1 gene, which encodes the extracellular matrix protein fibrillin-1. The FBN1 locus is situated at cytogenetic band 15q21.1 on chromosome 15, making this chromosome the site of the gene responsible for the hereditary disease.
